proof:
# Iid averaging of a uniform convex-body law

## Requested auxiliary statement

For independent uniform points `X,Y` in a `d`-dimensional convex body `K`, with centroid `g`, investigate whether

`P((X+Y)/2∈H)≥γ_d`

for every closed halfspace `H` containing `g`, and whether a sharper constant holds. This statement is not proved or refuted in this note.

The ordinary continuous theorem applied to the product body `K×K` gives only `γ_(2d)`, because the preimage of the halfspace under `(x,y)↦(x+y)/2` is a halfspace through the product centroid. This cannot be silently changed to `γ_d`.

## Exact failure of directional monotonicity

Iid averaging does not always improve each centroid halfspace's mass. Let

`K={(x,y):0≤x≤1, 0≤y≤h(x)}`,

where `h(x)=1+x` for `0≤x≤1/2` and `h(x)=3(1−x)` for `1/2≤x≤1`. The height function is concave, so `K` is a convex quadrilateral. Its area is one. The first coordinate of a uniform point has probability density `h` and mean `m=5/12`.

For the halfspace `H={x≥5/12}`, direct integration gives

`P(X∈H)=1−m−m²/2=143/288`.

For `1/2≤s≤1`, the CDF of the sum of two independent first coordinates is

`G(s)=s²/2+s³/3+s⁴/24−(4/3)(s−1/2)³−(1/3)(s−1/2)⁴`.

This can be obtained by writing the density in truncated-power form

`h(x)=1_{x≥0}+x_+−4(x−1/2)_++3(x−1)_+`

and convolving, then integrating. At `s=2m=5/6`, it yields

`P((X+Y)/2∈H)=1−G(5/6)=15343/31104`.

This is smaller than `143/288` by exactly `101/31104`. Both quantities still exceed `γ_2=4/9`; consequently this example blocks a monotonicity proof but does not refute the requested lower floor.

## Exact simplex obstruction to larger constants

For a simplex facet direction, one may normalize the corresponding uniform coordinate as `U∼Beta(1,d)`, with density `d(1−u)^(d−1)` on `[0,1]` and mean `1/(d+1)`. Thus the relevant averaged centroid cap is

`β_d=P(U+V≥2/(d+1))`,

where `U,V` are independent copies. Any universal lower constant for iid averaging is at most this value. Setting `a=2/(d+1)`, polynomial integration on the triangle `{u,v≥0,u+v≤a}` gives the exact finite formula

`β_d = 1 − d² Σ_(i,j=0)^(d−1) [ (−1)^(i+j) C(d−1,i) C(d−1,j) a^(i+j+2) i!j!/(i+j+2)! ]`.

In particular, `β_1=1/2` and `β_2=115/243`. Moreover, `dU` converges in law to a unit exponential variable, so `β_d→P(Gamma(2,1)≥2)=3/e²`. This limit follows from convergence of the independent pair and continuity of the Gamma distribution at the threshold; it is not a uniform lower bound for other bodies.

The cone values provide an exact test family, not a proof that cones minimize this nonlinear iid functional. Random concave-root calculations did not falsify that minimizer guess, but they supply no mathematical justification for it.

## Precise remaining issue

An improved product-body inequality, or a complete extremal theorem for

`∫∫ 1_{x+y≥2∫tf(t)dt} f(x)f(y) dxdy`

over densities satisfying concavity of `f^(1/(d−1))`, would settle this auxiliary statement. Neither an interchange of independent localization steps nor closure of a skewness order under convolution has been justified. The latter cannot simply be inferred from the concavity of each one-dimensional marginal.

Exact arithmetic for the directional counterexample and simplex formula is provided in `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_iid_averaging.py`.
